title: Cave Noire
subtitle: Konami · Game Boy

body: Cave Noire is Konami's Game Boy dungeon game about a new adventurer seeking a place in the guild of Karuzu. Four kinds of quest ask the player to defeat monsters, rescue fairies or collect a required amount of treasure. Each attempt creates another dungeon, making the destination a practical target rather than a fixed story route. The player has one chance to complete the assignment. A failed expedition leads to another layout, while success opens a harder version of the same kind of task.

Movement and combat proceed in turns, giving the player time to consider a position before committing to it. Adjacent opponents can exchange attacks, while items change the chances of surviving a dangerous room. A potion, spell or piece of equipment may provide a safer alternative to fighting every creature directly. The objective matters because clearing the whole dungeon is not always necessary. A successful expedition can depend on recognising when enough has been accomplished and choosing a route that avoids an unnecessary final risk.

Ten difficulty levels develop each quest type, with successful completions recorded between sessions. Equipment and the changing dungeon belong to the current attempt rather than a permanent character carried unchanged through every journey. Released only in Japan in 1991, Cave Noire gives the portable format a concise version of the roguelike idea. Its individual expeditions are small enough to approach as a single problem, while the saved ladder of harder assignments supplies a longer reason to return and apply what the last attempt taught.
story_headings: A short expedition with one clear objective
An enemy moves when the adventurer does
The game saves the achievement, not the expedition
